title: Design System: Marble Jar
source: Written after the Lamplight revamp shipped. Extracted from constants/lamplight.ts, lib/store.ts, components/lamplight.tsx, app/index.tsx, app/person/[id].tsx, app/_layout.tsx.

ground.purpose: Page canvas and the field fill on the shelf. Every screen's contentStyle.

board.purpose: Shelf boards, the quick-log composer, the trend board, closed-chapter banners. One step up from the ground.

board-raised.purpose: Selected state of a tag field — one step up from board.

hairline.purpose: 1px-3px borders, feed connector stems, the trend-to-split divider.

ink.purpose: Primary text on dark: names, counts, section headings, slip words.

ink-soft.purpose: Secondary text on dark: ledes, labels, ghost button text, vessel hint.

ink-faint.purpose: Tertiary text on dark: placeholders, quiet buttons, empty states, sort labels.

paper-deep.purpose: The slip surface when the moment was a removal.

paper-ink.purpose: Text and marks on paper: slip words, resting tag-field label and gloss.

cream.purpose: Brightest step, reserved for text sitting on cherry.

shelf-edge.purpose: The 5px bottom lip on a shelf board. Wood thickness, the only hard edge in the system.

paper-soft.purpose: The small meta line on a slip (sequence, tag, day).

cherry.purpose: Live actions only: + Kept one, Add, Save, the selected jar picker, the destructive confirm.

cherry-deep.purpose: Second step of removing a person from the shelf. Used exactly once.

honey.purpose: Reporting, never acting: positive trend bars, the week staff, validation hints, the fallback marble hue.

empty-ring.purpose: Stroke of an unfilled marble slot.

tag-boundaries.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-reliability.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-accountability.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-vault.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-integrity.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-non-judgment.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-generosity.purpose: BRAVING hue. Glass and tag edges only — never chrome.

tag-untagged.purpose: What a marble wears when its tag is unrecognized, so no-tag never reads as a tag.

display.purpose: The person's name as page title on the jar screen, 44px/46px. Also 30px for a shelf board's jar name.

headline.purpose: The shelf's opening question, 40px/42px. Also the native stack header title at 19px.

title.purpose: Section headings at 22px and week headers at 18px. No eyebrows or kickers exist in this world.

body.purpose: Karla 400 for all reading copy: fields at 16px, ledes 15px, meta and hints 12.5-14px.

label.purpose: Karla 600 for counts, field labels, chips and legends. Karla 700 at 15-16px is reserved for button labels so weight separates a tappable label from a static one.

hand.purpose: Caveat 600 for a moment's words on its slip (20px/24px) and the closing sign-off (24px). Nowhere else.

shadows.name: pin
shadows.purpose: Magnet pins on a slip and on a tag field. Smallest object, smallest falloff.

shadows.name: slip
shadows.purpose: Paper slips. The workhorse — every moment in the history feed carries it.

shadows.name: composer
shadows.purpose: The shelf's quick-log composer and framed control groups.

shadows.name: vessel
shadows.purpose: The glass jar — the tallest object, so the deepest falloff.

shadows.name: gloss
shadows.value: inset highlight rgba(255,246,224,0.75) at 34% of the dot diameter, offset upper-left
shadows.purpose: Not a shadow — the same lamp. Every filled marble dot wears one; unfilled slots get a 1.5px empty-ring stroke and no gloss.

motion.name: board-enter
motion.purpose: Shelf boards arriving on the shelf screen. Reanimated defaults; no custom easing token exists.

motion.name: marble-logged
motion.purpose: The single marble just logged, so a tap has a visible consequence.

motion.name: signoff-enter
motion.purpose: The closing 'Small moments, collected.' at the end of the feed.

motion.name: press
motion.value: opacity 0.75 (0.8 on tag fields), no duration token
motion.purpose: The only press feedback in the system. No scale, no ripple, no color shift.

breakpoints.name: column-cap
breakpoints.purpose: Both routes cap at maxWidth 880 and center. Above it the shelf reads as a bounded board; there are no other breakpoints — the layout is single-column at every width.

components.name: Primary Button — cherry
components.description: A live action. Fills the whole surface with cherry; used for + Kept one, Add, and Save.
components.css: .ds-btn-cherry { background: #C8452C; color: #FBF3E2; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; border: none; border-radius: 14px; padding: 15px 0; width: 100%; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 120ms; } .ds-btn-cherry:hover { opacity: 0.88; } .ds-btn-cherry:active { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-btn-cherry:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Ghost Button — hairline
components.description: The honest equal of the primary in the add/remove pair. Never styled as failure — no red outline, no warning icon.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { background: transparent; color: #D8BE98; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; font-weight: 700; border: 1.5px solid #503722; border-radius: 14px; padding: 15px 0; width: 100%; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 120ms; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #F5E9D2; border-color: #6B4A2E; } .ds-btn-ghost:active { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Text Field
components.description: A field is always one step darker than the surface it sits on. Focus is the caret plus ink text — no glow, no border shift.
components.css: .ds-field { background: #211410; color: #F5E9D2; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; border: 1px solid #503722; border-radius: 14px; padding: 13px 14px; width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; } .ds-field::placeholder { color: #A98F6E; } .ds-field:hover { border-color: #6B4A2E; } .ds-field:focus { outline: none; border-color: #A98F6E; }

components.name: BRAVING Tag Field
components.description: Full-bleed hue field. Each row floods with its own hue at rest; the chosen row goes dark and keeps the hue as a lit edge. Shown with one tag's hue; every other tag swaps only the --hue value.
components.css: .ds-tagfield { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; width: 100%; text-align: left; background: var(--hue); color: #2B1E11; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; border: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 14px; padding: 10px 14px; height: 44px; box-sizing: border-box; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tagfield-name { font-size: 15px; font-weight: 700; } .ds-tagfield-gloss { flex: 1; font-size: 12.5px; } .ds-tagfield-pin { width: 14px; height: 14px; border-radius: 7px; background: rgba(43,30,17,0.55); box-shadow: 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-tagfield:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-tagfield[aria-pressed='true'] { background: #372417; border-color: var(--hue); color: #F5E9D2; } .ds-tagfield[aria-pressed='true'] .ds-tagfield-gloss { color: #D8BE98; } .ds-tagfield[aria-pressed='true'] .ds-tagfield-pin { background: var(--hue); } .ds-tagfield:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Marble Dot
components.description: Fifteen slots make a jar at a glance. Filled slots wear the newest marbles' hues and a gloss; unfilled slots are a hairline ring. Shown at 15px (shelf) and 21px (inside the vessel).
components.css: .ds-marbles { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 7px; } .ds-marble { position: relative; width: 15px; height: 15px; border-radius: 50%; overflow: hidden; background: var(--hue); } .ds-marble::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 16%; top: 12%; width: 34%; height: 34%; border-radius: 50%; background: rgba(255,246,224,0.75); } .ds-marble.ds-empty { background: transparent; border: 1.5px solid #453019; } .ds-marble.ds-empty::after { display: none; }

components.name: Paper Slip
components.description: One moment, one piece of paper: a magnet pin in the tag hue, the words in handwriting, a meta line. The only light-colored surface in the product.
components.html:
Came back for the small thing I'd mentioned once

+1 · Integrity · Mar 4
components.css: .ds-slip { background: #F4E8CF; border-radius: 6px; padding: 10px 12px 12px; box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.35); } .ds-slip-pin { display: block; width: 13px; height: 13px; border-radius: 50%; margin-bottom: 6px; box-shadow: 0 2px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-slip-words { margin: 0; font-family: Caveat, cursive; font-size: 20px; line-height: 24px; color: #2B1E11; } .ds-slip-meta { margin: 4px 0 0; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; color: #6B5638; } .ds-slip.ds-removed { background: #EAD9B8; opacity: 0.82; } .ds-slip.ds-removed .ds-slip-words { text-decoration: line-through; text-decoration-color: #8A6F45; }

components.name: Shelf Board
components.description: One person's jar on the shelf: the name large, the count as a plain line, twenty dots. The 5px bottom lip is wood thickness, not a shadow.
components.html:
Maya

15 of 20 · 75%
components.css: .ds-board { background: #2C1D14; border: 1px solid #503722; border-bottom: 5px solid #170D08; border-radius: 20px; padding: 18px; margin-bottom: 14px; box-shadow: 0 5px 14px rgba(0,0,0,0.40); } .ds-board-name { margin: 0; font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 30px; font-weight: 700; color: #F5E9D2; } .ds-board-count { margin: 2px 0 0; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; color: #D8BE98; } .ds-dots { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 7px; margin-top: 12px; } .ds-board-actions { display: flex; gap: 14px; margin-top: 12px; } .ds-quiet { background: transparent; border: none; padding: 8px 6px; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: #A98F6E; cursor: pointer; } .ds-quiet:hover { color: #D8BE98; } .ds-quiet:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Pill Toggle
components.description: Sort, chapter and jar-picker chips. Selection fills with ink and inverts the label, so it reads as lamplight rather than as color.
components.css: .ds-pill { background: transparent; color: #D8BE98; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13.5px; font-weight: 600; border: 1.5px solid #503722; border-radius: 99px; padding: 9px 15px; cursor: pointer; transition: opacity 120ms, background 120ms; } .ds-pill:hover { border-color: #6B4A2E; } .ds-pill:active { opacity: 0.75; } .ds-pill:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 3px; } .ds-pill.ds-pill-on { background: #F5E9D2; border-color: #F5E9D2; color: #211410; }

components.name: Tag Dot Row
components.description: The shelf composer's compact alternative to the full-bleed tag field: seven beads, no fill, the hue only ever as a 2px selected edge.
components.css: .ds-tagdot { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; background: transparent; border: 2px solid transparent; border-radius: 99px; padding: 6px 9px; font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; font-weight: 600; color: #A98F6E; cursor: pointer; } .ds-tagdot:hover { color: #D8BE98; } .ds-tagdot:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #D9A441; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-tagdot-ball { width: 13px; height: 13px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--hue); } .ds-tagdot[aria-pressed='true'] { border-color: var(--hue); color: #F5E9D2; }

components.name: Week Chart
components.description: A bar chart, never a ring. Honey for a positive week, cherry for a negative one, a faint stub for an empty week. Appears only after two or more active weeks.
components.css: .ds-chart { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 10px; min-height: 120px; } .ds-bar { display: block; width: 20px; border-radius: 10px; } .ds-bar-up { background: #D9A441; } .ds-bar-down { background: #C8452C; } .ds-bar-zero { height: 4px; background: #A98F6E; opacity: 0.3; }

components.name: Stack Header
components.description: The native stack header: ground background, ink tint, no shadow. The board edge is the only divider in this world.
components.css: .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 14px; background: #211410; padding: 10px 14px; } .ds-nav-back { font-family: Karla, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 34px; line-height: 34px; color: #F5E9D2; cursor: pointer; } .ds-nav-back:hover { color: #D8BE98; } .ds-nav-title { font-family: 'Bricolage Grotesque', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 19px; font-weight: 700; color: #F5E9D2; }

narrative.overview:
Every surface in this product is one material under one lamp: warm enamel in deep espresso, catching light from above and behind. The shelf screen is a wooden shelf in a kitchen after dark — boards of darker wood laid on a darker ground, each jar a name set large, each marble a small glossy bead of colored glass. The jar screen is the same room from closer in, and it adds the only light-colored objects in the product: paper slips pinned to the board, carrying a moment's words in handwriting. Nothing else in the interface is allowed to be light-colored. The contrast between espresso chrome and paper slips is the whole visual argument: chrome is the room, paper is the life in it.

The system is dark-only and deliberately single-tone. Hierarchy comes from three steps of warm off-white ink (ink → ink-soft → ink-faint) over two steps of wood (board over ground), plus hairline borders. No screen adds a color beyond those, with exactly two exceptions that carry meaning rather than decoration: cherry red is reserved for live actions, and the seven BRAVING hues appear only as glass — marble dots, chart bars, split-track segments, tag edges.

Density is domestic, not airy. The history feed on the jar screen keeps a collector's density: real slips, one after another, grouped under a week staff, with sequence numbers (+1 / −1) printed on each. There are no placeholder cards, no icon tiles, no skeletons. An empty state is a sentence of plain copy, not a graphic.
keyCharacteristics: Espresso-and-paper: dark warm chrome, light paper slips, nothing between.
Three ink steps and two wood steps carry all hierarchy; hue never does.
Cherry red means "this action is live" — buttons and selection only.
The seven BRAVING hues are glass and tag edges, never chrome.
Circles for data (marbles, marks, pins), rounded rectangles for surfaces, near-square corners for paper.
Soft blurred black shadows as lamplight falloff; one hard wood edge per board.
Motion is arrival, not celebration: things fade and settle in.

rules.name: The Cherry Rule
rules.body: Cherry red fills the surface of a live action or a selected target — nothing else. It is never a border, a header, a heading, a divider, a data mark, or a decorative accent. If a screen shows no live action, it shows no cherry.

rules.name: The Glass Rule
rules.body: A BRAVING hue may appear as glass (marble dots, chart bars, split-track segments, legend dots, pins) or as the fill or lit edge of its own tag row. It may never color a board, a page, a header, a navigation element, a button, or a run of body text. Seven hues at once must never form a background.

rules.name: The Espresso Rule
rules.body: Every surface is a warm dark: ground, board, board-raised. There is no light theme and no neutral gray anywhere in the chrome. Light color means paper, and paper means a single moment's words.

rules.name: The Slip Rule
rules.body: A moment's words are always set in Caveat on paper. If a moment's reason is being read inside the chrome — never happens today — it would be a violation of the world, not a variant of it.

rules.name: The Three Ink Steps Rule
rules.body: Text on dark picks from exactly three inks: ink for what you read, ink-soft for what you scan, ink-faint for what is only there. Never introduce a fourth step or brighten an existing one for contrast.

dos: Do set a person's name in Bricolage Grotesque at 40–44px and let it carry the screen alone. Headings carry their own weight; there is no eyebrow, kicker, or overline anywhere in the product.
Do build hierarchy from ink → ink-soft → ink-faint and from board over ground before reaching for any other device.
Do give every Pressable an accessibilityRole, an accessibilityLabel that includes the count or state, and a hitSlop of at least 6px.
Do draw a removal as an honest mark: an open ring, a cherry down-bar, a darkened slip with struck-through words, and a −1 in the meta line.
Do reserve cherry for the surface of a live action or a selected target, and pair add/remove as two equal halves of one row.
Do fill a tag row with its own hue and keep the hue as the lit edge when the row is selected.
Do write a real sentence for empty states — "The shelf is bare. Add someone above — the first marble is a small kept promise away."
Do keep the twenty-dot row and the count line as plain text; the jar's state is legible without a single chart.
donts: Don't add a streak counter, score, achievement, progress ring, or leaderboard. The product's stated position is reflection over scoring; a count exists to be read, not graded.
Don't put a BRAVING hue on a board, header, button, or run of body text, and don't flood a surface with more than one tag hue.
Don't brighten the palette to fix a contrast problem. Fix it with the three ink steps, a hairline, or a shadow.
Don't render a moment's words in Karla, or a heading in Caveat. Chrome and handwriting never swap roles.
Don't use a hard offset shadow. The one hard edge in the system is a shelf board's 5px wood lip; everything else falls off with real blur.
Don't introduce a light theme or a neutral gray. userInterfaceStyle: automatic ships no light tokens, and it must stay that way.
Don't add icon-font or SVG glyphs. The product's only marks are circles, the typographic ‹, and the + / − on the log pair.

notCanonized: Lamp.good (#7FB069) is defined in constants/lamplight.ts and referenced nowhere in the build. Recorded as an unused token, not as a system color; do not inherit it.

app.json adaptiveIcon backgroundColor #E6F4FE, the splash background #ffffff, app/+html.tsx body #FAF7F0, and public/manifest.json theme/background colors are pre-Lamplight light-shell values that never went dark. They are app-shell surfaces, not product screens, so they are recorded here as drift and not as tokens.
